bull_bear.body:
- In-house R&D and reverse-engineering: 23 scientists/engineers (7.35% of permanent staff) driving prototyping and validation; R&D spend ~1% of revenue
- Three operating manufacturing facilities (two owned Lucknow plants commissioned 2018/2023, one leasehold Delhi-Bawana unit) with combined capacity of ~1,200 analysers and ~1.4 million reagent kits p.a.; ISO 13485:2016 and cGMP/QMS discipline
- Diversified IVD portfolio - reagents, instruments, consumables and AMC services across clinical chemistry, haematology, coagulation, HPLC, rapid/ELISA and molecular - marketed in ~26 states/UTs
- Technical collaborations with international OEMs (Elitech BV, Stago, other European partners) enabling Make-in-India instrument manufacturing to international quality standards
- 12-year brand build with promoter-led management: CMD Saurabh Garg has 31 years in healthcare/diagnostics; WTD Ajay Kumar Mahanty 20 years across sales, manufacturing and R&D
- Reagents-led model (56% of FY25 revenue) gives recurring consumable demand from installed diagnostic base
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic revenue concentration in Uttar Pradesh — UP alone was 72.25% of FY25 standalone sales (focus states 87%); regional disruption or procurement shifts hit revenue directly
- Working-capital intensity and rising leverage — Borrowings more than doubled to Rs 16,495 lakhs by FY25 (D/E 0.87 vs 0.58 FY23); Rs 11,000 lakhs of the issue is for working capital and Rs 9,000 lakhs for debt repayment - growth is balance-sheet funded
- Dependence on international technical collaborations (Elitech BV, Stago, other European partners) — Key instruments are manufactured to partners' specifications; loss or adverse change in tie-ups would stall the instrument segment and the Make-in-India pipeline
- Large traded (non-manufactured) instrument component — Rs 5,507 lakhs of FY25 instrument revenue was traded goods, exposing margins and availability to third-party/import supply
- Regulatory approval and compliance risk — Medonic M20 and KC1 Delta launches depend on pending approvals; facilities face periodic CDSCO/State Drug Authority/ISO audits - delays or adverse findings defer sales
- Extensive promoter-linked entity web and legacy guarantees — Numerous group companies with common directorships; Rs 1,060 lakhs corporate guarantee outstanding for divested associate POCT Science House; promoter-level litigation exists
- PAT decline despite revenue and EBITDA growth — FY25 PAT fell to Rs 2,813 lakhs (margin 8.97% vs 16.92% FY24) even as revenue grew 54%, signalling finance-cost drag on earnings quality
- COVID-era product demand normalization — Molecular/POC revenue built during the pandemic has largely evaporated, showing demand for some lines is not durable

business.body: Q-Line develops, manufactures and markets a diverse range of reagents (kits and POC devices) and consumables, and manufactures/imports/distributes diagnostic equipment, supplying since 2013 - directly or via distributors - mainly to diagnostic service providers, hospitals and medical colleges. Core IVD segments are Clinical Chemistry, Haematology, Immunodiagnostics, Molecular Diagnostics and Others (POC devices and Rapids); FY25 standalone revenue of Rs 31,371 lakhs split Reagents 56.27%, Instruments 36.64%, Consumables/Spares 4.47%, Service 2.62%. It runs a B2B model across around 26 states/UTs with exports, manufacturing from owned Lucknow plants and leasehold Delhi (Bawana) units, and makes analysers in India under technical collaborations with international companies.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Reagents:** Clinical chemistry reagents (64% of FY25 reagent sales), Haematology reagents (29%), Rapid/ELISA kits, HPLC reagents, Coagulation reagents, Molecular kits (RT-PCR, RNA extraction, VTM - COVID-era), POC strips, Microbiology reagents
- **Diagnostic Instruments:** Selectra Pro M medium-throughput fully automatic clinical chemistry analyser (manufactured under European collaboration), Clinical chemistry analysers, Haematology analysers, Traded analysers and POC devices
- **Make-in-India pipeline:** Selectra Pro XL high-throughput clinical chemistry analyser (prototype, with Elitech BV), Microlab 300 semi-automatic clinical chemistry analyser (prototype), Medonic M20 three-part haematology analyser (regulatory review), KC1 Delta coagulation analyser (with Stago, under review), InnoLyte electrolyte analyser (indigenous), Automated slide stainer (indigenous), Q-Count 5 five-part haematology analyser (under development)
- **Consumables/Spares:** Macro cuvettes with balls, Lab plastic plates, Laboratory plastic tip racks, Syringe pumps
- **Services:** Annual maintenance contracts on medical equipment sold

outlook.body: A fourth manufacturing facility, focused on reagents, at Plot C-42, Industrial Area Amausi, Lucknow is slated to begin operations in FY 2025-26 to support the growth trajectory; a further land parcel at KH-864 Amausi is held for future use. Existing capacity (~1,200 analysers and 1.4 million reagent kits p.a. across two owned Lucknow plants and leasehold Bawana, Delhi units) has been built up with plant & machinery additions of Rs 147.18 lakhs (2023), Rs 1,020.64 lakhs (2024) and Rs 334.89 lakhs (2025). Product-side expansion is via the Make-in-India analyser pipeline - haematology (Medonic M20, Q-Count 5), coagulation (KC1 Delta) and higher-throughput clinical chemistry (Selectra Pro XL) - pending validation/regulatory approvals; IPO proceeds fund working capital and debt repayment rather than plant capex.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Mix shift to instruments: instrument share of revenue rose from 21.4% (FY23) to 36.6% (FY25) as own-manufactured analyser sales scaled from Rs 611 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 5,987 lakhs (FY25) alongside traded units
- Reagents remain the recurring-revenue anchor (56.3% of FY25 revenue), led by clinical chemistry (64% of reagent sales) and haematology (29%)
- EBITDA margin expanded to 22.73% in FY25 (18.48% FY24) but PAT fell to Rs 2,813 lakhs from Rs 3,445 lakhs and PAT margin halved to 8.97% - finance-cost and below-EBITDA drag as leverage rose
- Balance-sheet-funded growth: total borrowings rose to Rs 16,495 lakhs (FY25) from Rs 7,365 lakhs (FY23), D/E 0.87 vs 0.58; IPO earmarks Rs 11,000 lakhs for working capital
- Post-COVID normalization: molecular reagent sales collapsed from Rs 678 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 19 lakhs (FY25) and POC from Rs 264 lakhs to Rs 9 lakhs
- Geographic concentration: Uttar Pradesh contributed 72.3% of FY25 standalone sales; five focus states 87% of revenue

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integrated into reagent manufacturing via in-house R&D (23 R&D personnel, 7.35% of permanent employees; R&D spend around 1% of revenue; reverse-engineering of components); instruments are both manufactured in India under royalty-bearing Technology Transfer Agreements with global/European diagnostic companies (Selectra Pro M with royalty payable; haematology reagents with royalty on RFID tags; Stago for the KC1 Delta) and traded/imported. Key raw materials (chemicals, cubitainers/caps and packaging; instrument components such as Power Supply PT535, data cable tree, panel PC, measuring unit, temperature control board; bulk reagent, antigen, antibody enzymes substrates) are sourced from domestic and overseas suppliers with no long-term supplier contracts (prices negotiated per purchase order); purchases FY25: domestic Rs 5,689.59 lakhs vs international Rs 8,680.93 lakhs (FY24: 3,941.83 vs 11,707.65; FY23: 2,553.02 vs 7,169.71), indicating import dependence for raw materials. Forward: B2B model selling mainly through distributors (over 397 in FY25) and directly to diagnostic service providers, hospitals and medical colleges, on a purchase-order basis, supported by 93 sales personnel and 37 service engineers/field managers; product delivery dependent on outsourced logistics partners. Also positioning as a full-service CMO/CDMO for IVD, having reduced costs and sourced EOL components for three clients.

concerns_observed: Promoter-entity distribution dependence is the dominant business fact: sales of goods to POCT Services - a partnership firm of promoters Saurabh Garg and Amita Garg - were Rs 19,747.85 lakhs in FY25 (~63% of revenue from operations), up from Rs 6,920.59 lakhs (FY23) and Rs 10,521.76 lakhs (FY24); the DRHP separately states the top two distributors were 68.19% of FY25 sales with the group entity alone above 60%.

Trade receivables from that same promoter firm jumped from Rs 0.37 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 3,228.01 lakhs (FY25) - ~39% of consolidated trade receivables - while total receivables tripled (Rs 2,644.36 to Rs 8,260.25 lakhs) and debtor days doubled to 96 (from 47): much of the FY25 revenue surge is not yet collected cash.

Operating cash flow is negative two years running: CFO Rs (128.45) lakhs FY25 and Rs (2,417.94) lakhs FY24 (vs +Rs 2,496.86 lakhs FY23); the FY25 figure also nets a Rs 4,462.82 lakh 'Investment in Fixed Deposits' classified inside operating working-capital changes.

Reported FY25 PAT fell 18.3% to Rs 2,813.09 lakhs (from Rs 3,444.47 lakhs) despite 54% revenue growth - dragged by an extraordinary Rs 1,696.52 lakh loss on selling the POCT Science House (associate) and Q-Line Nutraceuticals (subsidiary) stakes in the last two weeks of FY25, finance cost that more than doubled to Rs 1,470.00 lakhs, and Rs 156.36 lakhs interest on advance-tax shortfall; FY25 income also includes Rs 479.46 lakhs of sundry balances forfeited.

Stated RoNW of 23.74% for FY25 reconciles to PAT before the extraordinary loss (Rs 4,509.61 lakhs / Rs 18,994.53 lakhs); computed on reported PAT it is ~14.8% - the basis is not reconciled in the disclosure.

Leverage built quickly: total borrowings rose from Rs 7,364.84 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 16,494.98 lakhs (FY25; stated D/E 0.87 vs 0.60), including facilities priced up to 17.45% (IndusInd CC), 15-19% unsecured business loans and Rs 668.60 lakhs of on-demand unsecured promoter loans; Rs 9,000.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds goes to repayment.

Working-capital intensity keeps rising: audited-restated working capital of Rs 12,074.19 lakhs (FY25) is projected at Rs 19,143.27 lakhs (FY26) and Rs 27,976.22 lakhs (FY27) - the Rs 11,000.00 lakh IPO object funds only part of the build, with the objects unappraised by any bank or financial institution.

Royalty under the European technical collaboration escalated from Rs 17.79 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 502.71 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 1,586.97 lakhs (FY25, ~5.1% of revenue); the agreement is term-based with renewal not assured, and imports were 60.41% of FY25 purchases (74.81% FY24) - a structural cost and supply dependence.

Concentration on every axis: top-3 customers 71.50% and top-10 82.17% of FY25 revenue; Uttar Pradesh alone 72.25% (Northern region 80.50%); exports 0.09%; demand is tender/purchase-order based and cancellable without compensation, with no long-term supplier contracts - and the customer count declined in FY25 (1,005 to 963, or 989 to 948 depending on chapter) even as revenue rose 54%.

red_flags: Income-tax search and seizure/survey operations at the Company from September 2 to 5, 2025 - about three weeks before the DRHP date of September 30, 2025 - with books of account, records and documents examined/impounded/seized; no notices or assessment orders as of filing and the exposure is unquantified.

The two group-entity stake sales dated March 20 and March 24, 2025 (days before FY25 year-end) produced a Rs 1,696.52 lakh extraordinary loss against cash proceeds of just Rs 357.15 lakhs, with Rs 1,200.00 lakhs still receivable at year-end and the Rs 1,060.00 lakh corporate guarantee for the divested POCT Science House still outstanding.

Auditor annexure notes reliance on the management-determined list of Promoters/Group Companies without any verification procedure, alongside an internal inconsistency: the RPT note states no loans/advances were given to related parties while the same restated statements disclose receivables from Amit Agrawal (Rs 3.30 lakhs FY25) and former director Manisha Yadav (Rs 12.87 lakhs).

Companies Act trail: Section 42 private-placement breaches on three allotments (March 2019, June 2020, September 2021) now under voluntary ROC adjudication; Form CHG-1 charge filings not made for IndusInd Bank, Vivriti Capital, HDFC Bank and Tata Capital loans (Sections 77/86); cash-flow statements omitted from AOC-4 filings for FY17 and FY19; and director Manisha Yadav was removed w.e.f. April 18, 2024 with no reason stated.

strengths_observed: Scaled, fast-growing IVD franchise: consolidated revenue from operations grew from Rs 18,273.63 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 20,364.61 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 31,378.04 lakhs (FY25) - +54.1% in FY25 and a ~31% two-year CAGR - with EBITDA nearly doubling to Rs 7,132.12 lakhs in FY25 (margin ~22.7% vs ~18.0-18.5% in FY23/FY24).

Indigenous manufacturing depth unusual for an SME IVD player: in-house reagent manufacturing (ISO 13485:2016, ISO 9001:2015, cGMP across facilities, CDSCO/state/European agency audits since 2021) plus analysers made in India under a European technical collaboration; manufactured-instrument revenue scaled from nil (FY23) to Rs 611.00 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 5,987.15 lakhs (FY25), overtaking traded instruments (Rs 5,506.85 lakhs).

Broad announced product pipeline: Medonic M20 3-part haematology analyser (commercial sale expected Q4 FY26), KC1 Delta coagulation analyser via the Stago technical partnership, InnoLyte electrolyte analyser and automated slide stainer (commercial from H2 FY26), Selectra Pro XL and Q-Count 5 in development, Micro Lab 300 targeted FY27; a fourth, reagents-focused plant at Industrial Area Amausi (Lucknow) is slated for FY26 with CMO/CDMO positioning.

Distribution breadth beneath the concentration: sold through over 397 distributors to 963 customers in FY25 (828 in FY23; 361 customers placed repeat orders in all three years) across diagnostic service providers, hospitals and medical colleges in 26 states/UTs.

Capacity headroom without an IPO capex object: FY25 utilization of 49% (Unit 1, kits), 72% (Unit 2, instruments) and 45% (Unit 3, kits) on an aggregate installed base of 14.00 lakh reagent kits and 1,200 analysers per annum.
Disclosed return ratios in the 21-25% RoNW band across FY23-FY25 (23.74% FY25 as stated; see concerns on the computation basis) on a net worth of Rs 18,994.53 lakhs.

Entirely a fresh issue of up to 70,53,200 shares with no offer-for-sale component - Rs 9,000.00 lakhs earmarked to repay identified borrowings and Rs 11,000.00 lakhs for working capital, both accruing to the Company - and zero pledge on promoter shares.

Independent bench with senior-administration pedigree: 4 independents on an 11-member board, including two retired 1982-batch IAS officers (Rohit Nandan, former Chairman & Managing Director of Air India; Pravir Kumar, who held Secretary-level posts including MSME) and a former Revenue Service Principal Commissioner (Jai Prakash Singh).
